newsitem.title: UK: Britain denies backtracking on Hong Kong ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Britain denies backtracking on Hong Kong ceremony.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday denied it had backtracked by deciding to send two top officials to the swearing in of Hong Kong's new legislature after earlier insisting it would boycott the ceremony.
A foreign office spokesman said the two officials would be dealing with the Chinese authorities after the July 1 handover and it was important they should attend the ceremony.
But he said Britain would maintain its hard line on the new hand-picked provisional legislature, which will replace the colony's elected legislative council.
"This will not in any way imply approval of the setting up of the provisional legislature to which we remain adamantly opposed," the spokesman said by telephone.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will boycott the ceremony, but many of Britain's main partners have decided to send ministers.

The two officials attending the ceremony will be new Hong Kong consul Frances Cornish and Sir Hugh Davies, the senior representative to the Joint Liaison Group which will monitor the situation in Hong Kong until 2000.
"The inaugural ceremony will also include the swearing in of the chief executive, his senior officials and the judiciary," said the spokesman.
"(Cornish and Davies) will attend given that their work will bring them into close contact with the (new) Hong Kong authorities," he said. The U.S. consul to Hong Kong will also attend the ceremony.
